first_impression.reaction: My assistant shortlisted it, so it got a fair first screen. The opening line is the right register: 'two settings, not two standards' tells me nobody is trying to sell me the cheaper island. Calm, no exclamation marks, no deals. Her summary: Santorini is cliff-top suites, Mykonos is beachfront resorts with chapels; Katikies mentions hotel takeovers, Santa Marina sits on a private peninsula, the Myconian Collection has halal and kosher kitchens, Mykonos airport has a private flights lounge. Nothing states whether any of them holds 200 to 400. I read the venue lists, the guest experience section and the close myself, and skimmed the rest.

journey.quote: Choosing between a Santorini or Mykonos wedding is a choice between two settings, not two standards.
journey.reaction: Good. Quiet and confident. It assumes both are at the level I expect.

journey.quote: Katikies has Santorini properties in Oia, Imerovigli and Fira, and lists weddings and hotel takeovers among its event types.
journey.reaction: 'Hotel takeovers' is the only phrase on Santorini that speaks my language. My assistant flagged it.

journey.quote: Andronis Luxury Suites in Oia has suites and villas perched on the cliffs, looking across the Aegean to the volcanic caldera, and is home to the two-Michelin-starred Lycabettus Restaurant.
journey.reaction: Two Michelin stars. That is a welcome dinner my father would approve of.

journey.quote: A cliff-top suite hotel of intimate scale, with ceremonies high above the sea facing caldera sunsets.
journey.reaction: Honest, and it rules Grace out for us straight away. I'd rather know than find out on a call.

journey.quote: Santa Marina is a beachfront retreat on a private peninsula at the southern tip of Ornos Bay.
journey.reaction: A private peninsula is easier to close off than a cliff path in Oia. This is where my mind goes first.

journey.quote: Capacities, house rules and availability vary from venue to venue, and the view rarely tells you which spaces will hold your guest list.
journey.reaction: Correct, and not over-explained. But it means the page itself can't tell me whether either island takes 300 people.

journey.quote: Mykonos Grand states that both partners must be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on the hotel premises.
journey.reaction: Useful. Said plainly, without commentary. This is the kind of house rule my assistant needs before we waste anyone's time.

journey.quote: The Myconian Collection has certified halal and kosher kitchens and a South Asian chef for traditional Indian cuisine.
journey.reaction: Catering for a real family, stated as fact rather than as a gesture. This moves Mykonos up for us.

journey.quote: The airport also lists accessible travel information, parking and a Private Flights Lounge with VIP welcoming services.
journey.reaction: Finally, how our guests actually arrive. One line, and it's the right one.

journey.quote: A bus runs between Mykonos Airport and the town and other destinations, from a stop in front of the terminal at Arrivals, with tickets bought from the driver.
journey.reaction: Buses and tickets from the driver. Nobody in my family has done that. My assistant would skip this.

journey.quote: From May to October, expect high temperatures and large crowds at popular seaports.
journey.reaction: Crowded ports are not our concern. Fine for others, irrelevant for us.

journey.quote: Smartraveller also notes that Greece sits in an active seismic zone, with earthquakes and volcanic activity near major destinations including Santorini, and advises following local authorities.
journey.reaction: Our head of security will want this line. Better here than discovered later.

journey.quote: **You are planning a small wedding or an elopement.** Either island.
journey.reaction: There's a scenario for an elopement and none for a very large family wedding. I read the list looking for myself and I'm not in it.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos wedding questions, answered
journey.quote: Several venues publish wedding brochures or packages, including Canaves, Santa Marina and Grand Ambassador, and your inclusions should be set out in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Packages again, though only once and briefly. The sentence before it, about taking over a whole hotel, is the one I care about.

journey.section: Choose your island with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person throughout is right. 'For Australian couples' makes me wonder whether a family split between Dubai, London and Sydney is who they picture.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues can seat 200 to 400 for a reception, on either island?
Can Katikies Mykonos, Santa Marina or Saint John be taken over entirely for three days and closed to the public?
On Santorini, can a cliff-top property in Oia or Imerovigli be closed off at all, given the public paths along the rim?
Can our own security team work alongside the venue's, and how are staff phones and photography controlled?
Could the Myconian Collection's halal kitchen cater several days of events, including family customs, not just the wedding dinner?
Have they delivered a wedding at our scale on either island, and is there a private or referral route to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: Several venues publish wedding brochures or packages, including Canaves, Santa Marina and Grand Ambassador, and your inclusions should be set out in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: Package language in the cost answer puts me back in the standard-client queue, which is one of my main fears. It's mild here and only appears once, so it's a nudge rather than a deal-breaker.

turn_offs_found.quote: A bus runs between Mykonos Airport and the town and other destinations, from a stop in front of the terminal at Arrivals, with tickets bought from the driver.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining for a holidaymaker. With the ferry stairs and port crowds around it, the arrival section is written for guests who carry their own bags, which makes me doubt the page has guests like mine in mind. The private flights lounge line rescues it a little.

turn_offs_found.quote: **You are planning a small wedding or an elopement.** Either island.
turn_offs_found.why: The scenarios cover elopements but not a large family wedding. When the only size-related answer is 'small', it suggests a planner who doesn't think at my scale.

would_share_with: My assistant, to ask Santa Marina and Katikies about full takeover and reception numbers
My mother, for the Mykonos chapels and the Myconian Collection's halal kitchen
Our head of security, for the seismic, heat and wildfire lines

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start planning with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-or-mykonos-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet and the fee in writing up front is a mature touch. But I don't fill in web forms, and nothing here tells me they think at 300 guests. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: In 'Which island suits you', add a scenario for a large family wedding or a whole-property takeover that points to what the page already has (Katikies hotel takeovers, Santa Marina's private peninsula, the cost FAQ's 'take over a whole hotel'), so a big-family reader finds herself in the list next to the elopement scenario.

Trim the holidaymaker detail in 'Getting your guests there': cut or shorten the bus 'tickets bought from the driver' line and the seaport crowds line, and give the Private Flights Lounge line more weight.

In the cost FAQ, lead with the whole-hotel point and soften 'brochures or packages', and soften 'quotes in AUD for Australian couples' in the close so families spread across several countries don't read themselves out of the brief.

Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers

Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour, within a 5-minute budget.
Her family needs halal catering and includes an older relative; this fits the card's 'family customs' and 'catering' trust signals, but the card doesn't state it.
